previous.explanation_en: どこ asks which place or where. It is the place word in the Japanese コ・ソ・ア・ド series, alongside ここ, そこ, and あそこ.

parts.contribution_en: As a whole, asks which place or where.

sources.title: 何処（読み）ドコ - コトバンク（デジタル大辞泉・精選版 日本国語大辞典）
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen defines どこ as an indefinite demonstrative pronoun for an unspecified place or situation, and lists asking which place or part. It reports a historical sequence from いずこ through いどこ to どこ. The separate Nihon Kokugo Daijiten entry describes いどこ as an older form of どこ and cites an example from about 935; for どこ it cites a 1099 example transcribed with the reading トコ.

sources.title: 日本語 文法 どれ／どこ／どのN：カード - 東京外国語大学言語モジュール
sources.summary_en: The grammar resource places どこ in the place row of the コ・ソ・ア・ド series, corresponding to ここ・そこ・あそこ, and illustrates asking where a restroom is.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, どこ asks which place; Digital Daijisen classifies it as an indefinite demonstrative pronoun, and TUFS places it in the ド place row alongside ここ・そこ・あそこ.

The consulted dictionary entries report the historical chain いずこ → いどこ → どこ. The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten cites いどこ around 935 and a 1099 example under どこ, but transcribes the latter reading as トコ. These entries support reporting the dictionaries’ analysis; the cited examples alone do not independently establish the full sound history or demonstrate that the 1099 form was pronounced どこ.
Digital Daijisen also lists uses asking which part or what degree. Those are additional dictionary senses; the supplied definition and example concern place.

The 1099 citation is transcribed トコ, leaving the pronunciation relevant to the proposed transition to どこ unverified here. The J-STAGE PDF could not be retrieved for detailed inspection, so it is not used as evidence.
